newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-Harlequins name strong side for Auckland.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Harlequins name strong side for Auckland.

text.p: LONDON, Feb 17 - English rugby club Harlequins have named their strongest available team as they go searching for the prime scalp of Super 12 champions Auckland Blues tomorrow (NZT).

NZPA reports Harlequins will field six internationals, including England stars Will Carling and Jason Leonard, and Frenchmen Thierry Lacroix and Laurent Cabannes in a team which should provide a much sterner test for Auckland than that of Bristol last Thursday.
The Blues, in the first match of a three-game European tour ahead of their Super 12 campaign, swept a below-strength Bristol aside 62-21 on Thursday night.

Carling and Leonard are fresh from helping England to a record 46-6 win over Ireland on Saturday, but Ireland's captain Jim Staples pulled a hamstring in the match and so is not available for the cosmopolitan Harlequins, who also boast a Welsh international in lock Gareth Llewellyn and American Eagles hooker Tom Billups.
London looks set to turn on another wet day to make the pitch at The Stoop Memorial Ground even heavier than it is, but Auckland are still determined to turn on a display of running rugby.

Coach Graham Henry is adamant that, though he wants his team to win, it is more important for them to get players back in the groove of top-level rugby and in positive mood before heading for South Africa.
They face Northern Transvaal in their first Super 12 encounter on March 1.
For Harlequins, currently fourth in the English first division, the match is part of their 130th anniversary celebrations and is a rare chance to pit themselves against the world's best.
Rugby director Dick Best, the former England coach, said he won't mind his side being beaten if they can learn from the experience of facing Auckland.
"We found the European tournament a test, but a good learning experience in the autumn," said Best.
"Now we are going global and pitting ourselves against the top."
Auckland have also put in a strong side, although they are resting All Blacks skipper Sean Fitzpatrick.

The match will see the Auckland inside back combination of Junior Tonu'u, Carlos Spencer and Lee Stensness matched up again, while in the forwards it is another chance for loose forwards Mark Carter and Charles Riechelmann to push their credentials.
Andrew Roose will play at hooker in place of Fitzpatrick, who turned out against Bristol.
Henry said though the Auckland combination is strong, he is still not settled on a preferred lineup, and pointed out that several leading players will be joining the team in South Africa.

Harlequins: Steve Pilgrim, dan Luger, Peter Mensah, Dominic Chapman, Will Carling, Thierry Lacroix, Nick Walshe, Bill Davison, Laurent Cabannes, Alex Snow, Gareth Llewellyn, Rory Jenkins, Andy Mullins, Tom Billups, Jason Leonard (c). Reserves: Mick Watson, Paul Challinor, Chris Wright, Laurent Benezech, Paul Delaney, Simon Owen.

Auckland: Adrian Cashmore, Joeli Vidiri, Eroni Clarke, Brian Lima, Lee Stensness, Carlos Spencer, Junior Tonu'u, Charles Riechelmann, Mark Carter, Robin brooke, Richard Fromont, Leo Lafailii, Olo Brown (c), Andrew Roose, Orcades Crawford.
